title: You’re not lost.
paragraphs:
And deep down…
you know exactly why.

Because purpose terrifies you
more than failure ever did.

Because if God really has a calling on your life—
then you can’t keep living like this.

You say, “I’m just tired.”
But it’s deeper.

You say, “I’m just busy.”
But it’s heavier.

You say, “I’ll get serious with God later.”
But your soul knows—

Some of you are not confused about your purpose.
You’re just avoiding the surrender it requires.
Because purpose in God is never casual.

It will confront your pride.
Expose your hidden sin.
Break your self-made identity.
And rebuild you from the inside out.

That quiet conviction at night.
That pull when you hear the Word.
That discomfort when you try to ignore God.
That’s not guilt trying to destroy you.
That’s grace trying to wake you up.
But here’s where it gets real.

You’ve made peace with things
Jesus died to set you free from.

Secret habits.
Private compromises.
Silent addictions.

And you’ve learned how to function
while slowly disconnecting from God.

“See? This is who you are now.”
“You had your chance.”
“You’re disqualified.”
📖 “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” — Romans 8:1
That verse is not permission to stay the same.
It’s an invitation to come back.
Some scholars interpret this passage as emphasizing not just freedom from guilt, but freedom from the power of sin itself—through union with Christ.
📖 “For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works…” — Ephesians 2:10

You were designed on purpose.
With purpose.
For purpose.
And here’s the truth most people avoid:

You cannot walk in God’s purpose
while holding onto what nailed Jesus to the cross.
Jesus did not die for a future version of you.
He died for the real you.

The one struggling.
The one hiding.
📖 “But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
While you were still in it.

Not cleaned up.
Not fixed.
Not worthy.
That’s when He chose the cross.

Your sin was not ignored.
It was crushed.

Your shame was not minimized.
It was carried.

Your punishment was not delayed.
It was finished.

You are more sinful than you want to admit.
But in Christ, you are more loved than you can comprehend.
Repentance is not just saying sorry.

“Lord, I’m done pretending.”
“I’m done hiding.”
“I’m done being in control.”
📖 “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9

Not tomorrow.
Not “when things settle down.”

Because purpose is not found
in perfect people.
You don’t need a new life.
And His name is Jesus Christ.

The pride.
The secret sin.
The double life.
